sophia (arch): Quick sync—want to align on policy decision ownership and telemetry handoff for smart routing. I think we need an explicit contract: what the policy-engine returns, what runtime is allowed to do, and what telemetry we must emit.

mike (infra): +1. The big tradeoff is latency vs expressiveness. If we push more into the policy engine (remote service) we get richer rules but add RPCs. If runtime keeps logic, we increase footprint and rollout complexity.

anna (pm): Can we enumerate the concrete call/response shape we want? That will help product folks reason about rollout/visibility.

sophia (arch): Proposal sketch: policy-engine returns a compact decision object per request: 

```
RouteDecision {
  route_id: string,
  variant: string,      # e.g. quantized-llama, fallback-small
  score: float,         # for observability only
  explanation: string,  # short human token for explainability
  debug_token?: string  # one-time token to fetch full explain payload
}
```

Runtime MUST be able to apply deterministic local transforms: region overrides, tenant hard-constraints, and capacity-derived fallbacks. Anything non-deterministic (probabilistic sampling, global admission, heavy evaluation) should live in policy-engine.

neal (ops): Important: telemetry tags we emit for every decision: `policy_version`, `decision_path` (enum), `decision_latency_ms`, `route_id`, `tenant_id`, `region`, `policy_owner` (runtime|remote). We should also sample detailed traces (full explanation) at ~0.1% by default.

katie (eng): Agree on tags. Also want a local policy cache for offline/edge routing so we don't block on network. Cache entries should be signed and include `bundle_version` + TTL. Runtime should verify signature and reject stale bundles.

mike (infra): Implementation notes: cache + verification means we need a bundle format. Suggest a small compiled artifact: `policy.bundle.v1` which contains precompiled matchers and a minimal runtime lib. Runtime can evaluate quickly (~20-200us). Remote policy RPC only used for cache-miss / fallback.

anna (pm): How do we handle rollouts? If policy-engine returns new semantics, older runtimes might not understand new `explanation` fields etc. Backwards compatibility plan?

sophia (arch): Contract rules: 1) policy bundle must be backward compatible for at least two release cycles, 2) policy-engine responses include `policy_min_runtime_version` and `policy_bundle_requirements`. Runtime must refuse to accept a policy if it doesn't meet minimum. For hosted customers, we can orchestrate bundle rollout before turning default routing to new rules.

neal (ops): Telemetry cost: emitting the full `explanation` string every request is expensive. Use short codes for common reasons and keep a separate debug store keyed by `debug_token`. Sample full explanations into the debug store (0.1%) and on-demand via the debug token (requires permission).

katie (eng): What about explainability hooks for A/B and canary? We should include `decision_canary_tag` and a `trace_sampling_rate` per tenant in the bundle. Also add a debug endpoint: `/policy/explain?req_id=...&token=...` that respects RBAC.

mike (infra): Operational SLOs: decision eval 99th percentile < 2ms for in-process bundle eval. Remote policy call 99th < 15ms (we can budget retries/backoff). If remote call fails or times out, runtime must apply deterministic fallback policy (e.g., last-known-good bundle or simple region/cost-based heuristics).

anna (pm): For product: we need a clear UX in Console showing `policy_version` over time, % routed by variant, and sampled explanations. That will help debugging regressed quality after model/quantization changes.

neal (ops): Metrics to add now: `routing.decision.latency_ms`, `routing.decision.cache_hit`, `routing.decision.remote_failures`, `routing.decision.explain_samples`, and `routing.decision.fallback_applied`. All tagged with `policy_version`, `route_id`, `tenant_id`, `region`.

katie (eng): Security: signed bundles + key rotation. Also policy-engine RPC must authenticate with mTLS and include tenant-scoped tokens. Debug tokens should be short-lived and logged.

sophia (arch): Summary / action items I propose:
1) Draft short RFC defining the RouteDecision contract (fields above), bundle format (signed, versioned), and compatibility rules.
2) Define telemetry tagset and default sampling rates (0.1% trace, 5% explanation aggregates) and metric names.
3) Implement a minimal `policy.bundle.v1` prototype and runtime verifier + cache.
4) Add a Console panel for policy rollout visibility and sampled explanations.

mike (infra): Sounds good. I'll prototype the bundle shape and perf run.

anna (pm): I'll own the Console mockups and rollout playbook.

neal (ops): I'll write the metric/alert recipes (fallback spike, cache miss surge).

katie (eng): I'll pair with Mike on the runtime verifier + debug endpoint.

deploy-bot: deploy status: no deploys in last 24h.

sophia (arch): Great — I'll open the RFC and tag people. If anyone has strong objections to the `policy_owner` tag or bundle verification model, call it out here. Otherwise I'll start the writeup. :thumbsup:
